segments.title: Chương 4: Chạy bộ sáng
segments.content:
Chapter 4 Morning Run

Night fell. Jiang Nian took a shower and returned to his room, turning on the air conditioner before lying down on his bed. He opened the panel and, out of habit, smiled.

Although Jiang Nian's grades were average, as one of the main players on the school basketball team, he had been secretly running five kilometers every day for a whole semester just to show off during a full-court game.

Five kilometers in one go was like drinking water to him.

His plan was to wake up early tomorrow, run five kilometers first, then three, and finally finish with two. After all, he understood the principle of striking while the iron is hot, before one's energy wanes and is eventually exhausted.

After reviewing the mission, he pulled out his phone to check his bank account balance.

Money makes a man bold. The Jiang family wasn't particularly well-off; his grandfather had been in poor health a few years ago. They had borrowed a lot of money over the years and had only just finished paying off their debts this year.

As a result, Jiang Nian's allowance wasn't much, three or four hundred yuan a month at most.

But in just one afternoon, an extra thousand yuan had appeared in his account. If he finished the ten-kilometer run tomorrow, another two thousand yuan would land in his pocket, making it three thousand.

Money not spent is money earned in vain. He opened a shopping website, JD.com.

He was in his third year of high school. Even with a gaming company as a cover to legitimize the source of the money, his parents would still see earning money from games as putting the cart before the horse and delaying his studies.

Although a series of family inquisitions might be coming, Jiang Nian was thick-skinned and couldn't care less. Since the cat was already out of the bag, he might as well take the opportunity to go on a shopping spree.

For ordinary folks, the most direct way to save money was a two-pronged approach: buy fewer clothes and fewer shoes. Conserve water and electricity; don't buy new appliances, phones, or electronics unless the old ones break.

The Jiang family was no exception. Old Jiang and his mom hadn't gotten new clothes, shoes, or phones in two or three years. The TV and air conditioner at home were rarely turned on, and water from washing rice was used to flush the toilet.

Frugality is a virtue, but this kind of frugality was clearly just to save money. There was no quality of life to speak of; they were just tightening their belts to get by.

Clothes were hard to buy, and he couldn't afford phones or appliances, so he could only buy shoes.

Shoes were a necessity that could be had for a few dozen yuan, but the expensive ones, costing a few hundred, were expensive for a reason. He walked every day, so a good pair of shoes was very important.

Jiang Nian first bought a pair of leather shoes for Old Jiang for over five hundred yuan, then a pair of soft-soled sneakers for his mom for over three hundred. While he was at it, he bought himself two pairs of shoes for around two hundred yuan each.

The entire combo directly bottomed out the one thousand three hundred yuan.

He glanced at his balance: one hundred yuan.

Alright, time for bed.

Meanwhile, Jiang Nian's parents couldn't sleep.

The master bedroom was pitch-black as the couple had their nightly pillow talk. Things that were difficult to say in front of their child during the day could be discussed after the lights were out.

"Sigh, I just blinked and realized the kid's grown so much," Jiang Weizheng said, lying in bed with his hands behind his head, staring at the dark ceiling.

"He can even earn money now, and he cooked for us."

"What's so bad about Jiang Nian being a bit more mature? Why are you sighing about it?" Li Hongmei shot her husband a look in the darkness. "He used to cause trouble if you didn't give him a beating every three days."

"I'd love for him to be more mature, then I'd have less to worry about in the future. Right now, I'm just worried the money isn't from a legitimate source. If he goes down the wrong path at such a young age, he'll be finished."

"That's a bit much, don't you think? I know our boy, he has a sense of proportion," Jiang Weizheng said, pulling his hands back and frowning. "I looked up that gaming company. It's pretty big."

"I figure earning a bit of money each month should be fine. We just need to make sure he doesn't get too addicted."

The couple chatted quietly for a while longer but didn't reach a conclusion. As sleepiness set in, the thought of having to work tomorrow made them fall asleep.

The next day.

It was September. In the small southern county town, the sky was just beginning to brighten at five o'clock.

Jiang Nian woke up bright and early and changed into his running shoes. He subconsciously glanced at Xu Qianqian's apartment across the hall. The door was shut tight. Uncle Xu was on a business trip, so she was home alone.

Oh well, I'll be generous and get her some breakfast.

The early morning was a bit chilly. Dressed in a short-sleeved, quick-dry shirt, he got goosebumps on his arms from the wind as soon as he went downstairs. Before him was a not-so-bustling street lined with old, self-built houses. "Fuck."

Nancheng Middle School, on the running track, a figure was stretched infinitely long by the morning light.

Jiang Nian was drenched in sweat, his chest and back soaked through. Running wasn't strenuous, and it wasn't too hot in the morning, but a long run would inevitably make you sweat.

After finishing five kilometers, Jiang Nian's phone buzzed. He held it up and saw that his reward had arrived.

"Hey! It's here."

With a thousand yuan in his account, he twisted open a bottle of water from his backpack and chugged a few mouthfuls. He stood resting in the shade of a plane tree in the southwest corner, preparing to sprint the next three kilometers.

Not long after, the three-kilometer and two-kilometer runs were completed.

"xx Bank has received a transfer of 700 RMB 300 RMB."

By now, Jiang Nian was also a little out of breath. His entire body felt as if he had just climbed out of water, and the hair on his forehead was plastered down in strands, but his eyes were unusually clear.

He conservatively estimated that after some rest, he could run another five kilometers. Besides the high probability of not being able to get out of bed the next day, there were almost no side effects.

For some reason, Jiang Nian had no resistance whatsoever to training his legs.

He didn't have any grand ambitions. As a strong high school boy who'd been single since birth, his thoughts were the same as Mr. Ji Xianlin's in his youth: in this life, I only wish for more...

The autumn air was crisp and refreshing. The sun had just risen, and the sunlight on the streets was warm and clear. The morning light filtered through the gaps in the trees' branches and leaves, the Tyndall effect tracing the shape of the light.

Jiang Nian, holding his bicycle, managed to buy four servings of breakfast before eight o'clock.

The prices in the county town were relatively cheap. Shredded radish and vegetable buns were one yuan each, a cup of soy milk was one yuan, youtiao were one-fifty, and meat buns were one-fifty.

"Thirty in total. Here you go."

Ding! "Paid."

"Okay."

Breakfast cost thirty yuan in total, a huge bag full. Jiang Nian himself could eat four meat buns, two youtiao with soy milk, and two or three vegetable buns.

The two thousand he just got, plus the 161 remaining from yesterday, minus thirty for breakfast, left him with a total of 2131 yuan.

There were quite a few people carrying large bags of breakfast like Jiang Nian, but they were mostly elderly. They slept early and woke early, buying breakfast for their children and grandchildren who were heading to work or school.

The bicycle's wheels rolled over the dry road, the boy's soaring figure imprinted in the golden morning glow.

Screech. With a sudden brake, Jiang Nian jumped off his bike.

He carried the large bag of breakfast home, just in time to see his mom, Li Hongmei, getting up. Her hair was messy, her eyes filled with morning fatigue, and it looked like she was about to make breakfast.

Even though prices in Zhennan County were already very cheap, making breakfast at home was still more cost-effective.

Four yuan worth of rice noodles, with chopped millet peppers, green peppers, garlic, and scallions, mixed with a bit of chili oil, peanuts, cilantro, and pickled long beans, then drizzled with sauce, would make a filling meal.

The curtains in the living room were drawn, and the light was dim.

Li Hongmei was wearing her curtain-like mom-brand pajamas and slippers. She looked at her son, who had just walked in smelling of sweat, and the large bag of breakfast in his hand.

"You went to buy breakfast?"

"Yeah, I bought it on the way back from my morning run." Jiang Nian nodded, placing the large bag of breakfast on the table. "Mom, you don't have to work so hard. I'll take care of breakfast from now on."

(End of this chapter)
